about: What a link from a thread becomes when it's clicked: web (http or https with a host: opens in the browser without asking), ask (any other scheme starts another app, so only after Mike says yes to that link by name), file (handed to the app's file check) or refuse (nothing that can be opened). The copies: desktop/core/src/open_policy.rs link_kind (the desktop app), ios/ThreadbearKit/Sources/ThreadbearKit/LinkCheck.swift kind(of:) (read through URL(string:), where a string URL can't read is refuse), android-native/kit LinkPolicy.kt kind, and web/src/link-policy.ts classifyLink against a page at https://threadbear.example/t/abc (its never is refuse). Input is the link as written; expect is the kind. Not covered here, as only some apps have it: the desktop's file check (decide_file), the Convex sign-in page check (desktop convex_panel.rs and the Swift LinkPolicy.convexSignIn), and a refusal's words (the desktop cuts a long link in the middle there). Since Daybreak 167 (22 Nov 2026) every copy refuses, before the scheme, a link with a control, a format character (bidi overrides, zero-width ones: Unicode's Cf) or a line or paragraph separator, and a link that asks unless it's printable ASCII (no space, blank filler or wide letter) and 1,024 characters at most, so its question can show all of it, as it opens (the desktop's alert doesn't scroll); a web address may be up to 8,192 in the apps, 2,048 on the website. The iPhone's copy is LinkCheck.kind(of:), which applies that before LinkPolicy.swift (a byte-for-byte copy of the frozen Mac app's). Most differences are by design: the website is stricter (it runs in a browser), and the desktop, unlike a phone, opens paths.
